The 13:30 Daily Bias video, the first one in the new series, got 31 impressions on X, 11 views on YouTube and 3 on Facebook, with no likes or replies anywhere, even though the video runs almost 2 minutes. learned: The first Daily Bias video (13:30) drew almost the same small numbers as the other posts, so the series needs the question, not the length, to earn replies.
A plain "no analysis, no revenge trades" title again got the top YouTube views and likes, consistent with plain comparison and myth titles beating study-code titles.
The 7 tagged site visits since 1 Nov (3 facebook, 2 youtube, 2 chatgpt.com) show that tagged links work, but none has turned into a trial yet.
suggestions: Trials ending today (15:24 and 19:35 London) and Sunday (14:18 and 21:31): draft a short check-in note for those trialists (needs Max's OK and a send path); the 15:24 one is on the $799.99 yearly plan.
The $70 Perfect Entry charge that failed on 13 Nov will retry on 17 Nov about 01:46 London: consider a short card-update note to that member before then (needs Max's OK).

Nothing is queued in Buffer after the 14 Nov 18:00 posts, so schedule the next days of Daily Bias and engagement posts today, and end each Daily Bias caption with one reply-able question (for example "Strong, weak or sweep?") as the first line, not the last.

weekly_reviews.label: 7 to 14 Nov 2026
weekly_reviews.headline: Soft week. Reach about 1,108 across 53 posts, down about 68%.

numbers.reach_note: Down about 68% from about 3,492 the week before, which was carried by a 1,013-view Short. No post broke out this week. Links got 0 clicks.

weekly_reviews.best: One wick is not a body close was the only post that worked on all three channels (35 YouTube views, 68 X impressions, 44 Facebook, the only Facebook post above 11). When buy Demand ends led YouTube with 51 views. The 276 trades / profit factor 1.69 line led X with 99 impressions.
weekly_reviews.worst: A sweep is not proof of an edge had 7 YouTube views and 0 Facebook impressions. Code-led titles such as 3 candles outside had 11 YouTube views. Daily Bias Day 1 Part A at 110 seconds had 18 YouTube views, 31 X impressions, 3 Facebook, and no likes.
weekly_reviews.whop: Store visits 7 to 13 Nov: 281 (up from 146), but they slowed to 10 to 15 a day late in the week. Month to date: 406 visits. New trials 8 to 14 Nov: 3 (down from 7). 1 trial converted, at $0 on a promo. Revenue 8 to 14 Nov: $149.99 from 2 renewals, versus $54.99 the week before. MRR $2,007.54, 19 paid members. Free Master Class sign-ups: 0 since 1 Nov. No tagged trial or sale. One Perfect Entry $70 first charge has been past due since 13 Nov 20:36 London; retry 17 Nov about 01:46 London.
worked: Plain myth or contrast titles beat study-code titles. One wick is not a body close and When buy Demand ends led the week. Code-style titles got 7 to 12 YouTube views.
The 21:30 London slot. The top three X posts and the top Facebook post all went out at 21:30.
Number-first lines on X. The 276 trades / profit factor 1.69 post got 99 impressions on X and was a weak Short (20 views) under a different hook.
Specific, testable claims started a real conversation. A concept plus a clear question is still the all-time best post.
did_not_work: Facebook overall: 5.6 impressions a post, median 3, 0 comments. The 110-second Daily Bias went out as a feed video, not a Reel.
One-tap quizzes and stat images: 23 to 44 impressions on X and no answers.
Daily Bias Day 1 at 110 seconds: the same small numbers as everything else, no likes. Too long, and the question came last.
Links got 0 clicks, and no visit or trial could be tagged to a channel. Whop visits rose, but trials fell (3 versus 7).

next_week.label: 15 to 21 Nov 2026
next_week.goals: Fewer, better posts built around what worked: plain myth or contrast titles, number-first lines on X, chart-first prediction prompts with a same-day answer, and the strongest pieces in the 21:30 London slot. Daily Bias episodes cut to 55 to 75 seconds, with the question on screen in the first 2 seconds. Try it for free stays modest (only the two strongest 21:30 learning videos). Nothing is scheduled or sent until Max approves.
changes: Dropped Spot the Candle quizzes, the Which candle is hardest 1 to 4 quiz, weekly vote prompts, and stat-only posts.
18:00 is now the answer to the 09:00 chart prompt, on X only. Facebook keeps the 09:00 chart and the videos, not the weak engagement slots.
Titles rewritten in the myth or contrast style. Daily Bias titles no longer lead with a series prefix or a code.
X 21:30 captions lead with a number. Daily Bias target length is 55 to 75 seconds so it can run as a Facebook Reel.
Try it for free only on the Tue and Wed 21:30 learning videos. Numeric link codes stay as a proposal.
